name: ranger
version_context: Official ranger/ranger release ref v1.9.4 resolved to commit 55fc2839f693aed9486d211694d7317d78161341; bounded source snapshot, not a latest-release assertion.
summary: A Python curses file manager that maintains navigable directory/tab state, advances background loader generators cooperatively, and delegates previews and file opening to external programs.
scope: Concrete resolution of the generic file-manager target: ranger/ranger, GNU GPLv3 console file manager, distinct from Yazi
Directory hierarchy, selection, and tab cursor state
Cooperative loader and preview subprocess boundary
Architectural benefits and costs are inferences rather than measured performance claims

features.name: Tab-local navigation state over directory objects
features.description: Tab stores current directory/file, history, cursor pointer, path, and ancestor pathway. Movement and tab-change signals update the active file and restore the tab's saved pointer into the directory object. Selection returns marked entries when present and otherwise the current file.
benefits: Actions can consume a common selection interface for single and marked files
costs: Tab-local cursors must be synchronized with directory-object cursors
Saved navigation state does not freeze a filesystem that other processes can mutate

features.name: Cooperative generator loader
features.description: Loader::work takes the first queued loadable with a generator, unpauses it, and repeatedly calls next until completion, failure, or the work-time budget expires. A changed active item pauses the previous one. CommandLoader integrates subprocess work into this loader interface.
benefits: Generator steps provide a common incremental interface for copy and subprocess tasks
Time budgeting lets control return to the interactive loop between work intervals
costs: The budget is checked between generator steps and cannot preempt a blocking step
Queue priority, pause state, and external process behavior affect responsiveness

features.name: Preview subprocess and dimension-aware cache protocol
features.description: get_preview either opens text directly or queues the configured preview script with path, dimensions, cache-image path, and image-preview flag. Exit codes select dimension-specific text, reusable text, image, direct-image, no-preview, or fallback-text outcomes. The in-memory preview dictionary is keyed by real path and dimension pairs with wildcard dimensions.
benefits: Independent tools can add rich formats without embedding every decoder in the UI
Dimension-aware caching can reuse previews across redraws
costs: Preview behavior depends on installed tools and the script exit-code contract
Loading flags, caches, process completion, and current selection need coordinated updates

features.name: External file-launcher boundary
features.description: ranger ships rifle as its file launcher and routes execute_file through Rifle.execute with filenames and launch options. The official README distinguishes the file manager from programs selected to handle file types and lists optional external preview dependencies.
benefits: File browsing can reuse existing viewers and editors
Launch policy can vary independently of tab navigation
costs: Actual behavior depends on launcher configuration and executable availability
External applications have their own failures and side effects outside navigation state

mathematical_views.model: Navigation state machine over a changing directory graph
mathematical_views.question: How do tab switches, cursor movement, and marking determine the files an action receives?
assumptions: State contains each tab's path, history, pointer, current directory/file, and the directory's marked entries
Movement signals and tab-change signals are explicit transitions; selection prefers marked entries over the current file
The graph is an observed filesystem view, not an immutable tree: links, deletion, permission failures, and concurrent changes are outside the simple navigation model

mathematical_views.question: What does the loader's work budget constrain, and where can a job exceed it?
assumptions: Queued, active, paused, completed, and failed are abstract loadable states
A generator step is indivisible to Loader::work; the wall-clock budget is tested between next calls
A responsiveness bound requires a bound on each generator step and cannot be inferred from the budget alone
Subprocess execution can overlap independently, so this is not a claim that all system work is single-threaded

costs: Synchronization with shared directory objects and changing filesystem state

benefits: Incremental work with simple generator lifecycle
costs: Long steps can overrun the intended work interval

benefits: Rich previews through replaceable external tools

evidence.title: ranger 1.9.4 identity, design goals, and dependencies
evidence.notes: Inspected Python/curses identity, GPLv3 license, rifle composition, directory hierarchy UI, and optional preview dependencies. Official ref v1.9.4 resolved through the repository commit API. Chosen explicitly for the otherwise generic file-manager request.

evidence.title: Tab state, movement signals, and selection
evidence.notes: Inspected Tab initialization, move/tab.change handlers, at_level, and get_selection.

evidence.title: Generator-based loadables and cooperative work loop
evidence.notes: Inspected Loader::work; Loadable, CopyLoader, and CommandLoader definitions locate the generator and subprocess interfaces. Budget enforcement occurs between generator next calls.

evidence.title: Preview subprocess and cache handling
evidence.notes: Inspected get_preview including wildcard dimension lookup, loading flag, image mtime check, return-code cases 0-7, and CommandLoader callbacks.

evidence.title: File execution delegated to rifle
evidence.notes: execute_file documents launcher arguments and delegates execution to self.rifle.execute; no claim that the file manager implements the selected viewers.
